title: Lifting mixed comparison squares and their coherences to fixed pairs
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_i,\mathcal D_i$ ($i=0,1$) be categories in a common sufficiently large universe [def-nagata-category], with endofunctors $F_i$ and $G_i$. Let $J_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$, $T_s:\mathcal C_0\to\mathcal C_1$ and $T_p:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal D_1$ be functors. Give natural isomorphisms
$$b_i:J_iF_i\simeq G_iJ_i,\quad r_s:T_sF_0\simeq F_1T_s,\quad r_p:T_pG_0\simeq G_1T_p,\quad j:J_1T_s\simeq T_pJ_0,$$
where juxtaposition is ordinary composition, and assume for every $K\in\mathcal C_0$ that
$$r_{p,J_0K}\,T_p(b_{0,K})\,j_{F_0K}=G_1(j_K)\,b_{1,T_sK}\,J_1(r_{s,K}).$$
On fixed-pair categories [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], use the transports with structures $J_i(\theta)b_i^{-1}$, $T_s(\theta)r_s^{-1}$ and $T_p(\psi)r_p^{-1}$ and with the corresponding functors on arrows. They are functors, and $j$ lifts to a natural isomorphism
$$\widetilde j:\widetilde J_1\widetilde T_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde T_p\widetilde J_0$$
whose component at $(K,\theta)$ has underlying arrow $j_K$. In particular its precise intertwining identity is
$$j_KJ_1(T_s(\theta)r_{s,K}^{-1})b_{1,T_sK}^{-1}=T_p(J_0(\theta)b_{0,K}^{-1})r_{p,J_0K}^{-1}G_1(j_K).$$
The inverse has underlying arrow $j_K^{-1}$. These lifts preserve any specified identity and cocycle equations between composites of these transformations and their functorial whiskerings, provided those equations have the same source and target pair functors and hold on underlying arrows. The assertion applies equally when $T_s,T_p$ are inclusions of coefficient stages into common-stage categories, rather than scalar-extension functors; it requires no equivalence assumption on $T_s,T_p$ or $J_i$.

proof.text:
For any of the four transports, write its data as $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $U:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$, $V:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B$, $c:LU\simeq VL$. The proposed structure $\eta_X=L(\theta_X)c_X^{-1}$ has inverse $c_XL(\theta_X^{-1})$, since both composites cancel to identities by functoriality. For an intertwiner $u\theta_X=\theta_YU(u)$, naturality gives $LU(u)c_X^{-1}=c_Y^{-1}V(Lu)$, hence
$$L(u)\eta_X=L(u\theta_X)c_X^{-1}=L(\theta_Y)LU(u)c_X^{-1}=\eta_YV(Lu).$$
Thus the stipulated arrow map lands in the fixed-pair morphisms. It preserves identities and composition because $L$ does and pair composition is underlying composition. Apply this calculation with $(L,c)=(J_i,b_i),(T_s,r_s),(T_p,r_p)$ to obtain all four functors.

proof.text:
Fix $(K,\theta)\in\mathcal C_0^{F_0}$. Multiply the assumed mixed equation on the left by $T_p(b_{0,K}^{-1})r_{p,J_0K}^{-1}$ and on the right by $J_1(r_{s,K}^{-1})b_{1,T_sK}^{-1}$. Cancelling adjacent inverse factors, using that functors preserve inverse equations, gives
$$j_{F_0K}J_1(r_{s,K}^{-1})b_{1,T_sK}^{-1}=T_p(b_{0,K}^{-1})r_{p,J_0K}^{-1}G_1(j_K).$$
Both sides have source $G_1J_1T_sK$ and target $T_pJ_0F_0K$. No inverse of a functor has been used.

source.place: Agent expansion of returned proof step 8: rearranging the supplied mixed square

proof.text:
The two composite pair functors give structure maps
$$\alpha_K=J_1(T_s\theta)J_1(r_{s,K}^{-1})b_{1,T_sK}^{-1},\qquad \beta_K=T_p(J_0\theta)T_p(b_{0,K}^{-1})r_{p,J_0K}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $j$ at the underlying arrow $\theta:F_0K\to K$ is $j_KJ_1(T_s\theta)=T_p(J_0\theta)j_{F_0K}$. Substituting it and the preceding step yields
$$j_K\alpha_K=T_p(J_0\theta)j_{F_0K}J_1(r_{s,K}^{-1})b_{1,T_sK}^{-1}=\beta_KG_1(j_K).$$
This is the defining pair-morphism condition and, on expanding $\alpha_K,\beta_K$ by functoriality, precisely the displayed intertwining identity in the statement.

source.place: Agent expansion of returned proof step 9: naturality at the Weil structure

proof.text: From $j_K\alpha_K=\beta_KG_1(j_K)$, compose on the left with $j_K^{-1}$ and on the right with $G_1(j_K^{-1})$ to get $j_K^{-1}\beta_K=\alpha_KG_1(j_K^{-1})$. Thus $j_K^{-1}$ is the inverse pair morphism; the two composites are identities because they are so on underlying arrows. For a pair arrow $u:K\to K'$, the equality $T_pJ_0(u)j_K=j_{K'}J_1T_s(u)$ is naturality of $j$ and is also naturality in the pair category, whose forgetful functor is faithful. The inverse family is natural as well: compose this equality on the left by $j_{K'}^{-1}$ and on the right by $j_K^{-1}$. These families therefore define the required natural isomorphism $\widetilde j$.

source.place: Agent expansion of returned proof step 9: inverse and naturality

proof.text: For any specified equation with the same source and target pair functors, evaluate both sides at a source pair. Forgetting takes identity components to identities, vertical composition to composition, right whiskering to applying the underlying functor to the component, and left whiskering to evaluating the component on the transported pair. These assertions follow directly from the arrow maps in step 1 and the component formulas in steps 3–4; in particular they also hold for inverse components. Thus each component equality after forgetting is exactly the assumed underlying equation. Faithfulness of the forgetful functor makes the two pair arrows equal, and componentwise equality gives equality of the natural transformations. This proves the identity and cocycle assertions. Taking $T_s,T_p$ to be coefficient-stage inclusions makes the identical calculations with their stipulated $r_s,r_p,j$; none of steps 1–4 uses fullness, faithfulness, essential surjectivity, or any inverse functor.
